key_insight: A fixed hard-constraint projection layer improves a PINN for 1D Burgers’ flow by enforcing a local discrete approximation of the governing PDE.
engineering_relevance: This approach could improve the accuracy and physical consistency of neural flow models while reducing sensitivity to physics collocation-point selection.
method: Locally discretise the nonlinear 1D Burgers’ equation using a finite-difference stencil.
Decompose the discrete equation into constraint and prediction matrices to construct a projection.
Project PINN velocity predictions onto the discrete constraint set using a final, non-trainable layer.
evidence_signal: Initial tests on an unseen uniform grid show approximately an order-of-magnitude lower data error than a comparable PINN, alongside better PDE adherence.
watch_item: The projection enforces a discrete approximation, not the continuous PDE exactly; evidence is preliminary and limited to 1D Burgers’ flow.
paper_title: Hard Constraint Projection in a Physics Informed Neural Network (Burgers)
